source.text: Coordinators keep emailing the analyst to change thresholds for a practice. They want to do it themselves in Acme Claims, with a reason recorded.

questions.q: Who should be able to override a threshold: every care coordinator, or only coordinator leads?
questions.found: Today only Program analysts change thresholds, on the Program Configuration screen. Care coordinators can see thresholds on the member record but cannot change them.

questions.q: Should an override apply to one member only, or to the whole program for that practice?
questions.found: A threshold is set per program and applies to every attributed member in it. The Monthly program report and the quality heatmap both use the program threshold.

questions.q: Does someone need to approve an override before it takes effect?
questions.found: Contract changes in Acme Claims already go through an approver, who sees who changed what on the contract history screen.

questions.q: Should the payment and incentive figures use the overridden threshold, or keep the original?
questions.found: Incentive figures sent to the finance partners are calculated from the program threshold every month.

questions.q: How will the business know this works? One or two checks are enough.
questions.found: The BRD for threshold overrides (Confluence, version 4) lists two outcomes but no checks.
sug: Override shows on the member record
Audit history shows who and why

stories.t: Override a threshold from the member record
ac: A coordinator lead can enter an override with a reason
The override shows on the member record
The program analyst sees pending overrides
Rejected overrides do not take effect

stories.t: Show override history and use it in reports
ac: History shows who, when and why
Reports use the override where approved
